user_prompt:
A regular polygon of n sides is inscribed in a circle of radius 1.

What is the value of the limit of the perimeter of the polygon as the number of sides n increases to infinity?

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: The perimeter of a regular n-gon inscribed in a circle of radius 1 is P(n) = 2n·sin(π/n). Letting x = π/n, so that n = π/x and x → 0 as n → ∞, the limit is lim(n→∞) 2n·sin(π/n) = 2π·lim(x→0) sin(x)/x = 2π·1 = 2π. The limiting perimeter is 2π, which is the circumference of the circle.
